fact_check.claim: New student housing application opens April 1 (no time given)
fact_check.note: Page says the 2026-2027 new student application opens April 1 with no time; noon applies to graduate applications. 'Noon' was removed as asked.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's advice is to apply within ten days of receiving your NetID (transfers)
fact_check.note: Page: 'Transfer students should also apply for housing within ten days of receiving your NetID.' Article now calls it advice, not a deadline.

fact_check.claim: Confirmations begin mid-June: a building and room or the guaranteed waitlist with weekly updates
fact_check.note: Supported, including weekly emails for waitlisted students.

fact_check.claim: Common mistakes and FAQ: confirmations are 'rolling' and arrive 'by email, rolling through the summer'
fact_check.note: Page says confirmations begin mid-June and waitlisted students get weekly emails. It does not say all confirmations are rolling or sent by email.

fact_check.claim: Cannot start the application without an activated NetID
fact_check.note: Implied by the ten-days-from-NetID advice but not stated in the pages read.

fact_check.claim: Transfers may be placed in West Campus House System, South Campus Residence Halls, North Campus Residence Halls and Program Houses
fact_check.note: The fetch confirmed a sentence on this page that begins 'Transfer students may be placed in the West Campus House System' and continues past the quote limit. It did not return the rest of the list. The transfer page (new-transfer-undergraduates) does not list North Campus, so the article cites the application page for it, which is correct.

fact_check.claim: Transfer rooms grouped together when possible; transfers who qualify as first-years are placed in first-year residences in limited cases
fact_check.note: Both stated on the page.

fact_check.claim: West Campus houses: Alice Cook, Carl Becker, Flora Rose, Hans Bethe, William Keeton; Townhouse Apartments also on the list
fact_check.note: Houses match. Townhouse Apartments are a separate list item, and the article's wording ('also appear on the list') is accurate. It still sits inside the West Campus bullet, which the previous review asked to change.

fact_check.claim: South Campus: Cascadilla Hall, Schuyler House, Sheldon Court, 112 Edgemoor, 104 Mary Ann Wood Drive, 109 McGraw Place
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Program Houses are for first-year and upper-level students; Equity & Engagement Community is upper-level only; Risley, HILC, Loving House
fact_check.note: Matches. Preferences are listed on the application with a mission acknowledgement box.

fact_check.claim: More than 500 first-year and transfer students live in Program Houses each year
fact_check.note: Page: over 500 first-year and transfer students will live in these communities.

fact_check.claim: Two-year requirement for new undergraduates; transfers one academic year; spring transfers owe spring plus following academic year; meal plan required
fact_check.note: Matches the application page and the transfer page.

fact_check.claim: Exemptions: two years on campus at previous school, or matriculating as junior or senior
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Exemption is requested by logging in to the Housing application and applying for the exemption term, before signing a license
fact_check.note: Matches, including 'not after a license is signed'. The previously requested Housing Office contact for documenting an exemption (607-255-5368, housing@cornell.edu) was not added to the exemption text.

fact_check.claim: Housing Office takes questions at 607-255-5368
fact_check.note: Page gives 607-255-5368 and housing@cornell.edu.

fact_check.claim: Fall 2025 timeslot deadline August 1; new students moved in August 18 and 19; 2026 schedule not posted
fact_check.note: Page says it shows Fall 2025 details and has no 2026 schedule. The article labels these as 2025.

fact_check.claim: Requirement applies to students who arrived fall 2022 or later
fact_check.note: Page says 'starting with students arriving in fall 2022'. The sentence 'a new transfer is housed, but does not choose' is the writer's inference.

fact_check.claim: Double is $6,872 per semester ($13,744 a year) for 2026-27
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Triple or one-room quad $6,322 ($12,644); single or townhouse double $7,783 ($15,566); super single $8,298 ($16,595)
fact_check.note: All match. The page lists a separate 'Quad' row at $6,872 per semester, which the cost table still omits, as the previous review asked it to include.

fact_check.claim: Rates include gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet up to 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Meal plan is separate / 'meal plan not included' in the room rate
fact_check.note: The rate page does not mention meal plans. The application page says residents must enroll in one. Co-op page says four co-ops include meal plans.

fact_check.claim: Co-op singles $3,949 to $6,014 per semester; doubles $3,487 to $4,981
fact_check.note: Single range runs from Red Bud $3,949 to Wari $6,014, so the article's $6,014 is right. The previous review's $5,693 was the 302/308 Wait Avenue maximum. Doubles $3,487 (Red Bud) to $4,981 (660 Stewart, Wari).

fact_check.claim: Eight co-ops, among the least expensive options, most singles and doubles, four with meal plans, all with shared kitchens, selection from early February, rolling
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Co-op page says communities for transfer students and undergraduates after their first semester; transfer page says upper-level only
fact_check.note: Both statements are accurately reported and the conflict is flagged to the reader.

fact_check.claim: Common mistakes: 'Skipping the co-ops because they are not in the main application. They have their own process and their own prices.'
fact_check.note: No source says co-ops are outside the main application. The transfer page lists co-ops as upper-level only, so telling transfers not to skip them contradicts the article's own eligibility caveat.

fact_check.claim: You can request single, double, triple or quad; Cornell will do its best; roommate questionnaire or name a student, not guaranteed
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: New transfers cannot cancel; fee schedule ($50 through Jan 31 up to $2,000 July 1 to Aug 15) is for returning juniors and seniors
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: No-show rule: not checked in by first day of classes without arranging a late arrival means cancellation and 50 percent of the fall semester room rate
fact_check.note: Matches. The page says to arrange late arrival and to contact Housing directly.

fact_check.claim: Room change application open select times in fall and spring; Room Swap lets new transfers swap with sophomores, juniors, seniors, not first-years
fact_check.note: Page lists fall and spring room-change windows. The swap rule is in the Summer 2027 section: sophomores, juniors, seniors and new transfers swap with each other; first-years only with first-years.

fact_check.claim: All first-year students are guaranteed on-campus housing; the transfer page does not use the word guarantee
fact_check.note: Page says all first-year students are guaranteed. The transfer page text had no 'guarantee' wording.

fact_check.claim: Housing guides link (/housing/) in the exemptions paragraph
fact_check.note: The previous review asked for this internal link to be deleted unless the page exists. It is still in the article. No evidence the page exists.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential: one poster says transfers are placed after current students and most end up in a West Campus house; another says many went to Cascadilla and Schuyler
fact_check.note: Two posters are merged. Momofthree24 says transfers 'get placed after current students' and hedges that many went to Cascadilla and Schuyler ('I think'). HopefulHotelieMom says most transfers get West Campus housing and disputes the last-pick assumption. The article attributes the first two claims to 'one poster' and the Cascadilla claim to 'another', and leaves out that the posters disagree.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Sun 2016: some transfers temporarily housed in North Campus lounges
fact_check.note: Lounges in Jameson and High Rise 5 housed 30 transfers.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Sun 2018: transfers had no housing guarantee and some learned their assignment in June
fact_check.note: Freshmen guaranteed, transfers not; transfers not told until June 22.

beats_top.why: The top result is Cornell's own application page, which gives rules and timing but no rate table, no combined timeline, no co-op prices and no history of transfer placement. Our page answers the question in the first paragraph and covers all of those.

Add the $6,872 quad row and the Housing Office contact for documenting an exemption.
Drop the 'skip the co-ops' mistake or reword it to say co-ops are upper-level only.
